- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion and reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment turns negative.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is stable; use sentiment history to adjust for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to align with true mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral), model tends to forecast flat or slightly upward; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid false momentum.
